newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Analysts unruffled by FNB results.
newsitem.headline: Analysts unruffled by FNB results.

text.p: Analysts said on Wednesday that they were unruffled by a lower-than-expected earnings per share figure from First National Bank Holdings Ltd, South Africa's third largest bank by assets.
The bank posted a headline figure for the year to September 30 of 229.8 cents a share, up from 210.4 cents, but below the forecast range of 243-252 cents.
The firm's shares edged down five cents to 25.05 rand by 1305 GMT and, though the firm's stock price is near its year low of 24.50 rand, analysts said the results contained few real surprises.
"The market has been expecting this news. I think the stock is now a bargain at this price," said one banking analyst who asked not to be named.
The firm's results were hit by a bad debt charge that came in at 665.2 million rand, up from 393.5 million rand last time.
Analysts said most of this bad debt had come from its Wesbank car financing unit, with other contributions from its retail credit card operation.
They added that the bank was clearing out its operations and set for a good year in 1997. "The core businesses are in line," one analyst said.
